title: Queued request surge caused by stale routing config; mitigation & follow-up plan
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: On 2025-02-14 we observed a multi-region degradation that caused sustained SLO misses (p95 generation latency and error rate) for ~47 minutes. Root cause was a stale traffic-routing config pushed during a routine rollout that left a subset of frontend routers forwarding to a secondary region that had reduced capacity for our model clusters. The misrouting amplified queueing, delayed circuit-breaker tripping, and triggered aggressive load-shedding policies in a way that increased tail latency instead of protecting latency SLOs. This ticket documents the timeline, root cause analysis, immediate mitigations, and the action plan to prevent recurrence.
timeline: 2025-02-14T08:03:00Z - Alert: p95 generation latency > 1.5x baseline for several customers. Pager triggered.
2025-02-14T08:07:00Z - On-call runbook: checked per-region token throughput and saw secondary-region (eu-west-2) token rate spike while primary-region (us-west-2) dropped unexpectedly.

2025-02-14T08:11:00Z - Investigation: control-plane rollout log shows routing config version v2025-02-14-1 deployed 08:05Z. Canary passed on a small subset but validation skipped a routing-affinity check due to a flaky health-check job.

2025-02-14T08:18:00Z - Observed queue length in eu-west-2 frontend shards rising from 40->310 requests per shard; accepted requests exceeded provisioned workers leading to CPU throttling on model servers.
2025-02-14T08:23:00Z - Circuit breakers at the global proxy layer delayed open because the error-rate window required 60s and the spike had a fast ramp; this allowed backlog to amplify.

2025-02-14T08:34:00Z - Load-shedding policy in eu-west-2 engaged but mis-ordered evaluation with cache-warmup logic caused shedding of short requests that could have been served from KV cache, increasing outbound traffic and downstream retries.
2025-02-14T08:50:00Z - Manual rollback of routing config to v2025-02-13-9 executed; traffic gradually rebalanced and queues drained over next 12 minutes.
2025-02-14T08:58:00Z - Post-rollback monitors returned to baseline; incident declared resolved at 09:00Z after two stable cycles.
2025-02-14T09:15:00Z - Post-incident: initial RCA draft shared; follow-up actions proposed and owners assigned.
impact: 47 minutes of elevated p95 latency (1.5x baseline) and transient spike in 5xxs for ~12% of affected traffic. Several enterprise customers reported degraded experience; two customers triggered support escalations. Estimated cost impact: additional failover compute for the secondary region and retry-induced load ~4 hours of excess runtime across clusters.
root_cause: A routine routing-config rollout (v2025-02-14-1) contained a stale routing affinity mapping for a set of frontend shards. The canary step's automated affinity validation failed silently because the health-check job intermittently returned a 204 that the validator interpreted as success. The stale affinity caused an unexpected volume shift to a secondary region with less provisioned compute. Circuit-breaker thresholds and window sizes were tuned for slower-moving failures and therefore failed to open early enough, allowing backlog build-up. Finally, load-shedding evaluation order allowed cache bypass to happen before KV cache warmup decisions, which increased downstream retries and latency.
metrics: Peak queue length per eu-west-2 frontend shard: 310 requests (normal < 60)
Circuit-breaker open delay observed: ~120s from first elevated error to global open (target 30s)
Duration of visible customer impact: 47 minutes
action_items: Immediate (owner: Diego Ramirez) - Backfill and re-run the routing-affinity validator in CI to detect stale mappings; rollout fix in control-plane by 2025-02-18.

Immediate (owner: SRE Team) - Temporarily reduce global circuit-breaker error window to 30s and lower the open threshold for regional proxies during the emergency swimlane; revert when we have safe automated safeguards. Due 2025-02-20.

Short-term (owner: Claire Wong) - Reorder load-shedding evaluation so KV cache eligibility and warmup checks run before shedding decisions. Implement and validate via canary test harness. Due 2025-03-01.
Short-term (owner: Performance Eng) - Add a per-region capacity steering alarm that triggers when a region receives >70% of steady-state traffic unexpectedly. Create alert runbook. Due 2025-03-05.

Medium-term (owner: Aisha Patel) - Add routing-simulation unit tests in the control-plane PR pipeline that simulate weight drift and affinity changes to validate canary behavior. Include a synthetic traffic generator. Due 2025-04-01.
Medium-term (owner: Runtime QOL) - Implement circuit-breaker adaptive windows that consider rate of change (ramp detection) in addition to absolute error counts. Design doc due 2025-03-21.
Medium-term (owner: Observability) - Add end-to-end tracing span that tags routing-config-version on each request and surface top faulty config versions in Console. Due 2025-03-14.
Long-term (owner: Product) - Define a gating policy for control-plane routing rollouts that includes a synthetics plateau test before region-wide promotion. Proposal due 2025-04-15.
Follow-up (owner: SRE) - Run a fire-drill incident in a staging environment using the exact sequence to validate the new mitigations. Due 2025-04-10.
decisions: We will not change model capacity allocation immediately; instead we focus on preventing misrouting and improving detection logic.
Circuit-breaker tuning will be conservative and feature-flagged; adaptive windows will be implemented behind a flag and rolled out to limited regions first.
Routing validator failures are considered a hard stop for rollouts after the validator is hardened; interim failsafe to block canaries that report ambiguous health-check responses.
postmortem_notes: Primary lesson: small control-plane configuration drift can amplify into a region-wide incident when combined with tuned protections that are optimized for different failure modes.
We observed insufficient orchestration between routing, circuit breaking, and load-shedding layers; cross-team integration tests are required.
Good: on-call team executed rollback and runbook quickly; alerting captured the event and the console dashboards made root-cause signals visible within minutes.
Improvement areas: make canary validators deterministic, add synthetic plateau tests, and improve the ordering of protective heuristics.
